novelty.justification: The claim proposes a new mechanism/measurement hypothesis: a stop-decision circuit that “integrates commitment (answer decided) and verification-completion signals” and is “systematically biased toward late stopping (a learned safety margin).” Searches using “reasoning model internal stop circuit,” “end-of-thinking token mechanism,” “adaptive reasoning early exit confidence,” and “steering </think> token” identified Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models (2025), which self-truncates reasoning from answer confidence, alongside standard activation-patching and activation-steering work, but no retrieved work identifying the claimed dual-signal causal circuit. Moving from confidence-based adaptive stopping to causal localization and threshold steering is a non-trivial but natural extension using standard interpretability tools; the dual-signal integrator and learned safety-margin prediction provide substantive operationalization, but not clearly a new core relationship or general interpretability paradigm.
